articles.title: Quote of the Day by Miley Cyrus: “Anyone that hates on you is... – Inspiring lessons on confidence, positivity, resilience, jealousy and why the best revenge is massive success by the global pop icon known for her fearless individuality and deep insights on authenticity and criticism
articles.description: Quote of the Day by Miley Cyrus: Miley Cyrus’s quote, “Anyone that hates on you is always below you, because they’re just jealous of what you have,” explores the importance of self-confidence, resilience, and refusing to let negativity define your worth. The quote suggests that unnecessary hate and criticism often stem from envy or personal insecurity rather than anything lacking in the person being criticized. It encourages people to stay focused on their goals, value their achievements, and avoid being discouraged by negative opinions.

articles.title: Suneil Anand death reason: Dev Anand’s son and actor-filmmaker passes away in London at 70
articles.description: Suneil Anand, son of Dev Anand and Kalpana Kartik, has died at seventy. He passed away in London after suffering a heart attack on July twenty-sixth. Suneil Anand made his acting debut in his father's film "Anand Aur Anand" in 1984. He also ventured into filmmaking, directing the martial arts movie "Master" in 2001. The family has confirmed the news and requested privacy during this difficult time.

articles.title: ‘Ramayana’, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailers to Play With Tom Holland’s ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: Report
articles.description:
As excitement continues to build over the Ramayana trailer, word has emerged that it will be screened alongside Spider-Man: Brand New Day, set to hit theatres in India on July 30. Adding to that, the trailer for Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday is also set to accompany the same release. The news arrives after producer Namit Malhotra hinted that the trailer drop was imminent.

“We just announced, a while before the panel, that Sony Pictures Entertainment is going to be distributing Ramayana globally. That obviously means the trailer is hot on its heels. We showed the trailer at the panel, and I think we’ll be launching it very, very soon. So stay tuned,” he said in an interview with The Climax India.

The producer added, “It could be any day.”

Ahead of its release, the trailer, running past the two-minute mark, has already been leaked online, drawing excited reactions from fans over the introductory scenes of Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi.

‘Ramayana’, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailers

Film critic Taran Adarsh broke the news on his X (formerly Twitter) account, noting that both trailers would be shown ahead of the film’s screening.

“Moviegoers watching Spider-Man: Brand New Day in cinemas [from 30 July 2026] are in for an added treat... The theatrical trailers of Avengers: Doomsday and the much-awaited latest trailer of Ramayana will play before the film begins,” he shared in an update.

'SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY' ALL SET FOR A RECORD-SMASHING START – 'RAMAYANA', 'AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY' TRAILERS ATTACHED... #SpiderManBrandNewDay is all set for a massive opening in #India... And here's an #Xclusiv update.

Moviegoers watching #SpiderManBrandNewDay in cinemas [from 30... pic.twitter.com/NsvYvHLMDZ

Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s Advance Booking

The film has crossed 8 lakh tickets in advance sales on BookMyShow, pushing past the previous record set by Deadpool and Wolverine. Ticket bookings have picked up considerably in recent days, climbing from roughly 43,000 sold on July 17 to a high of 141,000 on July 26

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has already sold around 3.19 lakh tickets, bringing in a total of Rs 16 crore.

Brand New Day picks up the story after No Way Home, in a world where Peter Parker’s identity as Spider-Man has been erased from public memory. The film arrives five months ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, laying the groundwork for the next major superhero crossover. Doomsday, directed by the Russo Brothers, marks Robert Downey Jr’s return - this time suited in green rather than red, as he takes on the role of Dr Victor Von Doom.

articles.title: Morning Brief Podcast: Cockroaches, Courts & Committees: What Did India’s GenZ Really Win?
articles.description: We look back at the Jantar Mantar protests through the lens of media, technology and youth agency. What began as a Chief Justice’s jibe calling unemployed young Indians “cockroaches” turned into a movement that forced a Union minister’s resignation — powered by satire, memes and a 26-day hunger strike, and a social media following that outgrew the ruling party’s own. As the government rolls out fast-track courts, a tougher anti-cheating law and a Nilekani-led task force, the question is whether this marks a genuine break from the past or a repeat of 2024 — when a similar paper leak led to the Radhakrishnan committee's 101 recommendations, many of which remain only partially implemented two years on. Anirban Chowdhury speaks to Dr Anindya Kundu, sociologist, best-selling writer, Assistant Professor at Florida International University, Dr Usha Raman, former professor,Dept of Communication, University of Hyderabad and ET’s Anubhuti Vishnoi on virality, power, protest and reforms.
